name: Citizenship by Investment

requirements.blocker_text: Main applicant must be at least 18 years old.
Requires a non-refundable contribution to the Economic Diversification Fund starting at USD 200,000 for a single applicant, increasing with additional dependents.

Requires passing background checks and due diligence (USD 7,500 for the main applicant; USD 4,000 per dependent aged 16+), plus a mandatory interview (USD 1,000 per application) for applicants aged 16+.
Main applicant must be at least 18 years old.

Requires a minimum USD 200,000 investment in an Approved Project real estate development, held for a minimum of 3 years (5 years if resold to another CBI applicant), plus government fees starting from USD 75,000 per applicant.
requirements.fix_path: Fund the required real estate investment and government fees.

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Dominica's initial build. This is the country's flagship, highest-volume citizenship route and the reason Dominica is on this dataset's expansion shortlist. dual_citizenship_allowed set true: CBI applicants are not required to renounce prior citizenship, and Dominica's programme is explicitly marketed on dual-citizenship retention -- consistent with common knowledge of Caribbean CBI programmes and not contradicted by any source fetched. Modelled as two OR-logic groups (EDF vs. real estate) for the SAME 'Citizenship by Investment' status, per this dataset's core structural principle, rather than as two separate routes. physical_presence_requirement left null: no minimum days-in-country requirement was found in the sources fetched (a distinguishing, real feature of CBI programmes generally, but not independently reconfirmed for Dominica specifically here -- treated as an open point, not asserted as zero). The legal basis is the Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship Act 1978, ss.8-9, per cbiu.gov.dm's own legislation page, though the Act's PDF itself was not machine-readable in this pass -- the programme's operative terms are instead sourced directly from cbiu.gov.dm's current published guidance, which is itself the primary tier-1 government source for applicants.
